clue.text: Actively argued about photography pioneer

indicators.note: acting actively on the letters means they are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: about means concerning, the Latin-derived RE

explanation.surface: Someone argued energetically about an early photographer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actively' shuffles ARGUED together with RE (from 'about') to give the name. Louis Daguerre invented the daguerreotype, an early photographic process.
explanation.definitionFit: Daguerre was a French inventor whose daguerreotype process was among the first practical forms of photography.

clue.text: Nothing's the matter in work

parts.note: nothing is zero, the round letter O
matter here is the discharge from a wound, pus

explanation.surface: Asking what is wrong with a piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing's the matter' reads as reassurance; in fact 'matter' is the yellowish discharge from a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is the Latin word for a composition or creative piece, especially a numbered musical one.

clue.text: Write what St Ives used to have, in terms of galleries?

definitions.meaning: to write something down in a system of symbols

definitions.text: what St Ives used to have, in terms of galleries
definitions.meaning: the Cornish town once lacked a branch of the famous Tate gallery, read as two words

explanation.surface: A question about the Cornish art town and its galleries.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ives, a Cornish seaside town, got a branch of the Tate gallery in 1993; before that it had NO TATE, which runs together into a verb meaning write in notation.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to record music or other material in written symbols.

clue.text: Musical form — it's not a finale of concerto, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters have come to grief and fallen into a new order
a finale is the closing part, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A musical device is described as a poor way to end a concerto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges ITSNOTA into OSTINAT, and 'finale of' adds the last letter of 'concerto'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostinato is a phrase or rhythm repeated persistently throughout a piece of music.

clue.text: Very little support given to city repeatedly impounding a good deal of drug

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball before it is driven

indicators.note: impounding means shutting something up inside, so one piece goes within the other
repeatedly means the city's abbreviation is written out twice in a row

parts.note: NY is the usual abbreviation for New York City

indicators.note: most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: weed is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A tiny amount of help given to a city that keeps seizing large quantities of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles the city to NYNY, which is 'impounding' WEE; 'a good deal of' trims WEED by its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeny-weeny is a playful reduplication meaning tiny or minuscule.

clue.text: Prominent player giving curious look about notice

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a leer is a sly or suggestive sideways glance
an ad is a notice advertising something

explanation.surface: A star performer gives a strange glance at a posted announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: LEER goes 'about' AD.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of an orchestra is its principal first violinist, a prominent player.

clue.text: Radio fitting — here an op may be broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Listening equipment through which a staged opera might be transmitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be broadcast' looks like a radio term in a radio clue; it rearranges HEREANOP.
explanation.definitionFit: An earphone is a device fitted to a radio or similar set so it can be heard privately.

clue.text: Turns out English prisoners (not against starting that)

indicators.note: not tells us one word is taken away from another
the removed word is at the start of the longer one

parts.note: convicts are people serving prison sentences
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: England releasing prisoners with a parenthetical aside about opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as an aside, but it is the instruction: 'not' removes 'against' from the start ('starting that') of the prisoners, leaving VICTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel tenants from a property, to throw them out.

clue.text: R Tees flowing round in two channels

indicators.note: a flowing river moves its waters about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: The River Tees running around a bend, as if in two streams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing' rearranges the five letters into STERE. The Tees is a river in north-east England, and the clue's 'R' is the river abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stereo sound is reproduced through two separate channels to give a sense of space.

clue.text: Takes heart out of staying power

definitions.meaning: removes the innards of, as in preparing a fish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes heart out of' looks like 'discourages', but here it is literal: removing the internal organs.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to disembowel a fish or animal; the other is the informal word for courage and determination.

clue.text: One who greatly enjoys a story, with no time to take on business

indicators.note: with no tells us the following letter is taken away

parts.note: fiction is an invented story
ado means fuss or business, as in much ado

explanation.surface: Someone who loves a tale but has no time to take on business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no time' drops T from the story, leaving FICION; 'to take on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is an enthusiast or devoted fan of an activity.

clue.text: No opening to allegory promoting cultivation

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a parable is a short allegorical story

explanation.surface: An allegory without an introduction that encourages farming.
explanation.walkthrough: PARABLE loses its first letter P ('No opening to').
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is suitable for, and used for, growing crops by ploughing.

clue.text: It brings dubious figures out to be given a hearing

definitions.text: It brings dubious figures out to be given a hearing

parts.words: It brings dubious figures out to be given a hearing
parts.note: a vehicle carrying suspects to court for trial, not something exposing questionable numbers for discussion

explanation.walkthrough: A Black Maria is a British police van used to transport prisoners; 'dubious figures' are shady people, and a 'hearing' is a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: The police van takes suspects and prisoners to court for their hearings.

clue.text: Thirteenth line of seats turned in hardwood — collaborative effort

indicators.note: in places the turned row inside the timber

parts.note: teak is a tropical hardwood
M is the thirteenth letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: turned means read backwards

parts.note: a row is a line of seats in a theatre

explanation.surface: Row M of seats is made of hardwood, in a story about cooperation.
explanation.walkthrough: In theatres, rows are lettered, so the thirteenth is row M; M and WOR (ROW 'turned') go 'in' TEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Teamwork is combined, cooperative effort by a group.

clue.text: Card game with small amount going to West before East

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second
in an across answer, heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: a trace is a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A card game where small stakes move round the table from west to east.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, 'going to West' means reading right to left, so the small amount gives ECART; 'before' puts it ahead of E.
explanation.definitionFit: Écarté is a two-player card game of French origin.

clue.text: Treacherous character-to wit, unfortunately, not entirely simple

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters have met with mishap and been jumbled
not entirely means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: mere means simple or nothing more than

explanation.surface: A traitor is described, with a wry aside that the matter is not so simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges TOWIT into TWOTI; MERE ('simple') loses its last letter ('not entirely') to give MER.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-timer is someone who deceives a partner by secretly seeing another.

clue.text: Someone affected rose up in agitation

indicators.note: agitation stirs things up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A pretentious person jumps up in a state of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in agitation' rearranges ROSEUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur is a person who behaves affectedly to impress others.

clue.text: Plant reared on middle of street

parts.note: reared means rose up, as a horse does

indicators.note: the middle letters are taken, dropping the first and last

explanation.surface: A plant was grown in the centre of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'on' puts the first piece above the second; 'middle of' strips the outer letters of 'street'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose tree is a rose bush trained into a standard with a tall single stem.

clue.text: Tension and severe worry after day one's passed

indicators.note: passed suggests these letters have gone away, so they are removed

parts.note: distress is acute anxiety
the numeral one is written as the letter I

explanation.surface: Tension and anxiety linger once a day has gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: DISTRESS loses D and I ('day one's passed').
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is mental or physical strain and pressure.

clue.text: Boot company one time producing loose-fitting item

parts.note: to boot someone is to sack them from a job
a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A footwear firm, at one point, made a baggy garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boot' looks like footwear; it means dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack coat is a loose, straight-cut jacket without a waist seam.

clue.text: Show of hesitation after play's opening depicts battle scene

indicators.note: after puts the hesitation sound behind the play's opening

parts.note: Act I is the first act of a play
um is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: An opening scene with hesitant actors depicts a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play's opening' looks like its first letter P; it is ACT I, followed by UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Actium was the site of the naval battle in 31 BC where Octavian defeated Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Nonsense about initially young one being like a lad

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: bosh is old-fashioned slang for nonsense

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the numeral one is written as the letter I

explanation.surface: Silly talk about a youngster acting like a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: BOSH goes 'about' Y (first of 'young') and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyish means characteristic of a boy, youthful and lively.

clue.text: Book is closed with lover finally entering caf

indicators.note: entering means one piece going inside another

parts.note: a door that is to is closed

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A book is shut with a sweetheart arriving at a café.
explanation.walkthrough: A door pushed to is closed, so 'closed' can mean TO; 'lover finally' gives R, which is 'entering' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, inexpensive restaurant or café; caf is short for café.

clue.text: Has dinner after tea on board, showing consistency

indicators.note: on, in the sense of aboard, puts the meal inside the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship; being on board means inside it

indicators.note: after places dining behind the tea

parts.note: taken as written
has dinner means dines

explanation.surface: Someone eats dinner after tea on a ship, keeping to a steady routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords use SS (steamship) for a ship, so 'on board' places the tea and dinner inside S...S.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadiness is the quality of being even, regular and consistent.

clue.text: To reduce drug will make you attractive

parts.note: to cut is to reduce or lower
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Advice that cutting down on drugs will make you prettier.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the usual crossword abbreviation for ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means charming and pretty to look at.

clue.text: Mark on stave almost split

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: cleft means split, as in a cleft rock

explanation.surface: A mark on a musical staff is almost torn in two.
explanation.walkthrough: CLEFT ('split') loses its last letter ('almost').
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the symbol at the start of a musical staff fixing the pitch of the lines.

clue.text: International group backed by pleasant girl

indicators.note: backed by means supported from behind, so the second piece follows

parts.note: the EU is the European Union, an international grouping
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: An international union supported by a nice girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed by' looks like a reversal; it just puts NICE behind EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunice is a female given name.

clue.text: Magician, mostly unhappy invoking goddess, mostly

indicators.note: invoking means calling in, so the goddess is brought inside the other word
mostly means the word is used except for its last letter

parts.note: sorry means sad or wretched

indicators.note: again most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: Ceres is the Roman goddess of agriculture

explanation.surface: A magician, glum, calling on a goddess for most of the spell.
explanation.walkthrough: SORR (SORRY 'mostly') takes in CERE (CERES 'mostly') to give SOR-CERE-R.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorcerer is a wizard who practises magic.
